plans.buy_case: PYPL is flashing classic mean-reversion setup: RSI 35 (oversold), price pinned to lower Bollinger Band, and golden cross already formed with price above 200MA. Volume surge on weakness suggests institutional accumulation. However, low VIX (14.4) means complacency is masking risk—stay tight on exits.
plans.entry_condition: Enter on one of two triggers: (1) RSI dip to 28–30 on intraday weakness (higher conviction), or (2) immediate entry at current price if volume sustains above 3x average into market open. Do NOT chase if price rallies >2% without pullback.
plans.exit_condition: Take profit at 56.80 (upper BB, ~6% gain) OR RSI breaks above 60 with volume fade (loss of momentum). Hard stop: break below 51.10 (200MA support) closes position immediately—max loss ~$17/position.
plans.timeframe: 2–4 weeks. If not profitable in 3 weeks, reassess; mean reversion should show legs quickly.
plans.risk: Fundamental headwinds not yet visible (earnings miss, guidance cut, fintech competition). VIX complacency means a macro shock could cascade fast. Position sizing ($376) limits damage, but be ready to cut at -3% if technicals break first.
plans.additional_note: This is a *technical* setup, not a fundamental story. You lack fresh earnings/guidance—that's the real gap. Use this as a tactical 4-week swing, not conviction hold. If PYPL reports before your exit, reassess fundamentals immediately.

plans.buy_case: WRB is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI 39.3 in oversold zone, price pinned to lower Bollinger Band with active squeeze, and MACD histogram turning up—all with the 200MA filter intact. Low VIX complacency creates tactical opportunity, but fundamentals require verification before committing capital.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 30–32 range OR price to touch lower BB (≈$67.50). Do NOT chase at current price. Confirm MACD histogram stays positive on next candle.
plans.exit_condition: Sell 50% at 71.50 (50MA resistance); trail stop on remainder to 69.50 if BB widens and RSI breaks above 65. Exit immediately if price closes below 200MA (68.84) on high volume—mean reversion failed.
plans.timeframe: 2–4 weeks. If no movement by week 3, exit and redeploy—capital efficiency matters at $3.2K portfolio size.
plans.risk: Fundamentals unknown: earnings misses, underwriting deterioration, or macro insurance headwinds could break the mean-reversion thesis. Low VIX can spike fast, and financials are rate-sensitive. Position size ($342) is prudent, but WRB could gap down 5–8% on bad news.

plans.buy_case: L is showing classic mean-reversion setup: RSI 34.6 in oversold zone, price pinned to lower Bollinger Band, and MACD inflection—all within a healthy 200MA uptrend. The Bollinger squeeze suggests volatility compression before a move, offering asymmetric risk/reward for a swing entry.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 25–28 range or price to touch the lower Bollinger Band ($108.50–$109.00). Do not chase current price. Confirm MACD histogram remains positive or crosses above zero on entry bar.
plans.exit_condition: Sell 1/3 at RSI 60–65 (first profit target), exit remainder if: (1) RSI breaks above 70 and closes below it on high volume (momentum trap), (2) price closes decisively below 200MA, or (3) hold exceeds 6 weeks with no follow-through—cut at breakeven or 2% loss.
plans.risk: Low VIX (14.4) signals complacency; a surprise earnings miss or macro risk-off could invalidate the setup fast. L is a conglomerate with complex underwriting exposure—missing recent earnings/reserve data is a red flag. Position size ($329) limits damage, but conviction should drop if you haven't reviewed Q3 earnings and insurance loss ratios.
plans.note_to_busy_student: This is a textbook technical setup, but do *not* buy without 15 minutes of diligence: pull the latest 10-Q, check underwriting profitability, and glance at reserve trends. Financial stocks can gap down on disclosure. If fundamentals look stable, enter on the dip, manage tight stops, and move on—this shouldn't require daily monitoring.
